title: The shelf-photo check
scenario:
A drinks brand pays shops to place its new cans at eye level. Field staff send 30 phone photos a week. You set up an AI vision model to review them. The brand manager sends you this wish list for the model.

The exhibit shows the wish list and the state of this week's photos.
exhibit:
Wish list
  A. Is our logo visible and facing the front? (yes/no)
  B. Exactly how many cans are on the shelf? (for payment)
  C. Which staff member is in the photo? (name)
  D. Is this photo AI-generated? (fraud check)

This week's photos
  - 6 photos are sideways
  - 4 photos are HEIC files from phones
  - 3 photos are tiny thumbnails, under 200 px

questions.prompt: Which wish-list item is the best fit for the vision model?

options.text: B, because counting is simple for a computer.
options.explanation: Claude and OpenAI both list counting as approximate. A payment needs an exact number, so a person should count.

options.text: C, because the model can see faces.
options.explanation: Claude's docs say it cannot be used to name people in images and refuses to do so.

options.text: A: a yes/no check that the logo is visible and facing the front.
options.explanation: Right. Describing what is in an image and answering a clear visual question is what vision models are built for. A person still spot-checks.

options.text: D, because an AI model knows AI images best.
options.explanation: Claude's docs say it cannot determine whether an image is AI-generated and should not be relied on to detect fakes.

questions.prompt: Before sending this week's photos, what should you do?

options.text: Nothing. The model handles any file as it is.
options.explanation: Models have file-type and quality limits. Rotated and tiny images are listed weak spots.

options.text: Rotate the sideways photos, convert the HEIC files to JPEG, and ask for new photos to replace the thumbnails.
options.explanation: Right. Vendors list rotated and very small images as error risks, and Claude and OpenAI do not list HEIC as a supported type.

options.text: Shrink all photos to thumbnails so they cost less.
options.explanation: Smaller saves tokens, but Claude's docs say images under 200 pixels raise the error risk.

options.text: Send only the sideways photos, because the model can turn them.
options.explanation: Vendors warn that rotated images cause mistakes. Rotate them first.

questions.prompt: The model must compare each shelf photo with the brand's planogram (a picture of the correct shelf layout). How should you set up the prompt?

options.text: Send both images with labels, such as "Image 1: planogram" and "Image 2: shop photo", then ask what differs.
options.explanation: Right. Several images can go in one request. Claude's docs suggest a short label before each one so the prompt can refer to them by name.

options.text: Describe the planogram in words and send only the shop photo.
options.explanation: It can work, but you lose detail. The model can read both images, so send both.

options.text: Send the two images in two separate chats and compare the answers yourself.
options.explanation: The model can't compare images it never sees together. Put both in one request.

options.text: Merge both images into one wide panorama.
options.explanation: OpenAI lists panoramic images as a weak spot. Two labelled images are clearer and need no extra editing.
